The **Primary Option** elevates the prose into a sophisticated, literary style while preserving the raw, passionate intensity and every specific detail of the original. The **Secondary Option** offers a slightly smoother, more polished tone.

### Option 1: Literary & Poetic Elegance (Recommended)

> You love a woman, yet you wonder where she vanishes all night in some customized taxi, adorned in her high heels, her corset, and her bold, expressive lips. You cherish how she wears her glasses only in your presence—how, with soft, wide-eyed earnestness, she swears that yours is the only face she ever wishes to behold. You love her so intensely that you crave her altered, even distorted: if she is magnificently full-figured, you wish her delicate and frail; if she is gracefully slender, you wish her expanded like a cosmonaut. How could one fail to love her—her rich complexity, her bright vibrancy, her bouillabaisse, her orangina? 
>
> When you accompanied her to the physician, even the doctor marveled, “Look at that!” And you swelled with foolish pride—arrogant, perhaps, but that is simply the nature of your devotion. Any observer of the human form can discern her rarity, how her beauty eclipses everyone else. Yet your love for this woman is profound; why can no one perceive it? The rest of the world must suddenly grow blind to beauty if you are to keep her. You refuse to forfeit anything of her, ever. You desire her intimate perfection for yourself alone; you wish everyone else not blind, but perhaps rendered immobile—paralyzed from the eyes down. 
>
> You ponder where she spends her nights. If she leaves you, you will comprehend the true, devastating scope of love. And if she is leaving you now, you already do.

---

### Option 2: Refined & Professional Tone

> You are in love with a woman, and you constantly question where she goes throughout the night in an extravagant taxicab, wearing her high heels, her corset, and her striking, vocal presence. You treasure that she reserves her glasses strictly for you, swearing with wide-eyed devotion that you are the only one she desires to see. You love her so deeply that you desire her in her most unadorned state: if she is grand and voluptuous, you want her slender; if she is lithe and perfect, you want her enlarged, floating like an astronaut. How could anyone not love her, with all her unique flavors—her bouillabaisse, her orangina?

You want her intimacy entirely to yourself, wishing the rest of the world not blind, but paralyzed from the neck down.

For you to retain her forever, the rest of humanity would need to suddenly become entirely incapable of discerning grace or charm. You refuse to surrender the slightest piece of her, ever. You want her pubic area shaved smooth, and you wish that everyone else could keep their vision while suffering complete physical immobility from the neck down. 

You remain consumed by thoughts of where she vanishes to until dawn. If she ultimately walks out on you, the full reality of love will finally be made clear to you. And if her departure is taking place at this very second, you possess that painful knowledge already.

Here is an expanded, prose narrative based on your bullet points:

***

I loved her with a ferocity that bordered on absolute devastation. It was not a gentle or quiet affection, but a consuming, physical hunger that dictated the rhythm of my days. I desired her in every possible form—in the quiet stillness of dawn, in the fiery heat of passion, and in every shared touch that left me desperate for more. To be near her was to be completely submerged; her presence was my anchor, and her body, the only geography I ever wished to explore.

Yet, even in the depths of our profound physical closeness, a bitter poison took root. Darkness always brought a quiet terror, for it was during the late hours that she would slip away into the night, wrapped in a mystery she refused to yield. As I lay awake in the empty bed, listening to the ticking clock, my mind became a battleground of suspicion and anxiety. Where did she go? Whom did she see? The silence of her late-night outings echoed louder than any confession, gnawing endlessly at the edges of my sanity.

This relentless fear of loss twisted my devotion into something dark and possessive. I found myself harboring a desperate, selfish wish: I wanted the rest of the world to go blind to her. I wished that humanity were somehow rendered incapable of perceiving her extraordinary grace and breathtaking features. If only her beauty were invisible to everyone else, she would be safe. She would be mine alone, removed from the predatory eyes of a world that I knew would inevitably try to steal her from me.

And yet, my torment was deeply conflicted. When we stepped into the light of day, and I watched the world react to her, a strange, toxic pride warred with my paranoia. Her presence was undeniably disruptive; she had a way of commandingly altering the air in any room she entered, drawing turns of heads and quiet gasps. To see others acknowledge how remarkably striking she was filled me with a vanity I could not suppress. I was proud to hold the hand of a woman who could stop time for strangers, even as every admiring glance from a passerby struck a match against the tinder of my jealousy. 

In the end, the inevitable came to pass, and the shadow I had tried so desperately to outrun finally swallowed us whole. She left. 

It was only in the vast, suffocating silence of her absence that the final, devastating epiphany struck me. All my passion, my paranoia, and my feverish attempts to possess her had been mere shadows of the real thing. I realized then that a true, complete understanding of love is not forged in the warmth of embrace or the triumph of possession. It is only fully comprehended through the agonizing experience of its departure—when you are left alone in the wreckage, forced to measure the exact, crushing weight of what has been lost.

You watch her walk across the room, bathed in the soft, golden light of the late afternoon, and a dark, shameful knot twists tight in your chest. You do not merely adore her; you are terrified of her. She is too bright, too complete, too effortlessly magnetic for a world full of hungry, searching eyes. In the quiet, desperate corners of your mind, a monstrous urge takes root: you wish she were lesser. 

You find yourself entertaining absurd, vicious fantasies born not of malice, but of pure panic. You wish you could strip away the radiance that draws the gaze of strangers. You dream of cutting off her cascading hair, of dressing her in heavy, shapeless rags, of smudging soot across her perfect skin so that her beauty becomes invisible to everyone else. You imagine a world where she is flawed, marred, or diminished—because if she were broken, no one else would ever try to pull her from your orbit. You would be her only sanctuary, her only witness, her sole protector. It is a grotesque paradox: you love her with a devotion that borders on religious worship, yet you long to degrade her simply to guarantee that she stays. 

You want to build a vault around her and lock the door, hiding her in the dark so the light of the outside world can never entice her away. You hate the way the sun shines on her, because it reminds you that the sun belongs to everyone, and so, ultimately, does she. 

Yet, these desperate, obsessive thoughts do not spring from a desire for control; they are the thrashing, pitiful reflexes of a man who knows he is powerless. You do not wish to hide her because you possess her, but because you know, deep in your bones, that you are already losing her. 

The impending heartbreak is no longer a distant phantom—it is a cold draft creeping under the door. You feel it in the subtle shifts of her body language, in the way her hand lingers a fraction of a second less in yours, in the quiet, drifting distance that fills her eyes when she looks past you toward a future you aren't part of. The terrifying truth settles in: your possessiveness is not a sign of strength, but the preemptive grief of a man watching his entire world slip through his fingers.

It is only here, standing on the agonizing precipice of abandonment, that you finally understand the true, brutal nature of what you feel. Before the threat of her departure, love was a pleasant warmth, a quiet background noise of comfort and affection. But now, illuminated by the harsh, clarifying light of imminent loss, it has transformed into a blinding, suffocating fire. 

You realize the terrible secret at the heart of human devotion: love never reveals its true weight, its rawest and most overwhelming essence, when it is safe. It is only when the threat of devastation looms—when you are forced to measure the exact shape of the void someone will leave behind—that you realize how completely they have consumed you. You have never loved her more fiercely, nor felt her value more acutely, than in this excruciating moment: right as she is preparing to walk away.
outputs.L5:
**The Architecture of Becoming: You, How, and When**

Every great transformation, every quiet victory, and every bold step into the unknown rests upon a simple, three-part foundation. It is an equation of human potential that governs how we move through the world, shaped by three fundamental words: *You*, *How*, and *When*.

### **1. YOU: The Anchor of Agency**
Everything begins with *You*. In a world filled with endless noise, opinions, and distractions, it is easy to forget that you are the central actor in your own life. You are the holder of your dreams, the bearer of your challenges, and the sole owner of your choices. Circumstances may set the stage, but you choose how to play the part. Realizing the power of "You" means accepting accountability—recognizing that while you cannot control everything around you, you retain absolute authority over who you choose to be. Without your intent, no plan can take root.

### **2. HOW: The Strategy of Action**
Once you claim ownership of your path, the question naturally shifts to *How*. "How" is the bridge between a vision and reality. It is the realm of curiosity, strategy, and resilience. "How" does not demand that you have all the answers from the very beginning; rather, it asks that you be willing to learn, adapt, and iterate. It is built through small habits, consistent effort, and the courage to fail forward. Where "You" provides the desire, "How" provides the discipline. It transforms abstract aspirations into concrete steps. 

### **3. WHEN: The Catalyst of Now**
Yet, even the strongest resolve (*You*) and the best-laid plans (*How*) are meaningless without the final spark: *When*. The most dangerous trap in life is waiting for the "perfect" time—a mythical moment when fear vanishes and success is guaranteed. The truth is that conditions are rarely ideal. "When" is not a date on a calendar that you passively wait for; it is a decision you actively make. The most powerful answer to "When?" has always been, and will always be, *now*. 

***

### **The Intersection**
Life comes down to how these three elements interact. 
* If you have *You* and *How*, but no *When*, you are trapped in perpetual preparation—always planning, never starting. 
* If you have *How* and *When*, but no *You*, you are merely going through the motions, executing someone else’s script. 
* If you have *You* and *When*, but no *How*, you have passion without direction.

It is only when all three align that momentum is created. **You** are the author. **How** is the craft. **When** is the moment you put pen to paper. 

Don't wait for the world to move first. Decide who **You** want to be, figure out **How** to take the first step, and decide that **When** begins right now.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a prose poem about intense, obsessive, and possessive love using the second-person point of view.
counterfactuals.output:
I have memorized the precise geography of your shadow, the way it spills across the floor like wet ink, always dragging itself back to me. When you enter a room, the atmosphere folds in on itself, consuming every memory I have ever held until there is nothing left but the sharp, electric scent of your skin. I trace your silhouette onto the insides of my eyelids so that even in the pitch-black of sleep, I am forced to look at you. You are the only geometry that matters, the only light my eyes are permitted to break upon.

I am jealous of the sun for touching your neck before my mouth can. I am jealous of the very air that slides down your throat, reaching into deep, dark places my fingers will never touch. I want to swallow your voice whole, to trap your laugh behind my teeth so no one else can ever hear its bright, careless music. You believe you still belong to yourself, to the mundane rhythm of your days, but you are mistaken. You were claimed long before you knew you were being watched; I am the cage that grew around you while your back was turned.

If you took a blade to your own chest, it would be my heart that stopped. I have braided your name into the quietest currents of my blood, a relentless, quiet pulse: *mine, mine, mine*. There is no version of this world where you walk away intact, because I have already stolen the space where your breath meets the room. You cannot turn around without stepping into my shadow. You cannot bleed without spilling my name. And if you broke yourself to pieces just to escape me, I would collect every jagged shard of you and rebuild you into a mirror that reflects only my face.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Give me a piece of flash fiction in the literary style of Richard Siken—frenetic, sensory-rich, and exploring the paranoia of losing someone you adore.
counterfactuals.output:
Tell me you’re not going anywhere. Say it into the crook of my neck so the sound gets trapped under my shirt. 

Look at you: sleeping with your jaw soft, your collarbone catching the pale, bluish wash of the television screen, completely undefended. You think the ceiling is going to stay up. You think the floor isn’t going to open its mouth. It’s infuriating, how brave you are. It’s reckless. Outside, the rain hits the glass like thrown gravel, and I am sitting at the edge of the mattress counting the seconds between your exhales. One, two, three. If I stop counting, the rhythm breaks. If the rhythm breaks, the house fills up with cold water and we drown in our sleep.

There are too many sharp corners in this room. There are too many bad intersections in this town. 

While you were brushing your teeth, I made a list of every way a body can break. A stray tire flying off a semi-truck on Interstate 95. A tiny clot, quiet as a mouse, moving through the dark plumbing of your leg. A left-turn signal that doesn't light up. The universe is a dangerous, unlit parking lot and you walked right into the middle of it carrying the only light I have left. 

I press my thumb into the soft dip of your inner wrist, hard enough to feel the quick, wet jump of your blood against my skin. *Still here. Still here. Still here.* But tomorrow you have to buy coffee. Tomorrow you have to cross a street. Tomorrow you’re going to step into a box made of thin, cheap metal and drive sixty miles an hour past strangers who don't love you at all, who wouldn't even swerve if you stalled out in the lane. 

Wake up. Come on, open your eyes, wake up so I can watch you exist. 

I want to nail the doors shut. I want to swallow the keys. I want to drag my forehead against yours until we run out of oxygen in the exact same second, so neither of us has to sit alone in the quiet afterward. Don’t look at the window. Don’t look at the clock—it’s just a countdown, it’s just a teeth-grinding little machine telling us how much time we’ve wasted being separate. 

Listen to me. Put your hands where I can see them. The dark is full of quiet, greedy things, and they’re just waiting for me to blink.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a monologue about a man who loves his partner so intensely that he secretly wishes she were unattractive to the rest of the world just so he could keep her safe from everyone else's gaze.
counterfactuals.output:
*(He sits on the edge of the bed in the dim, amber light of a single lamp. He’s staring at his partner while she sleeps, his hand hovering just an inch above her cheek, terrified to wake her, but unable to pull away.)*

Look at you. Just lying there, completely oblivious to the chaos you cause in me. 

*(He lets out a soft, breathy laugh, shaking his head.)*

When we were at dinner tonight… I saw them. I always see them. The waiter who lingered just a second too long taking your drink order. The man at the corner table who kept glancing over his wife’s shoulder. The women who adjusted their posture when you walked past. It’s like the air in the room shifts every time you move. People just… pull toward you. Like gravity.

And I hate it. God, I hate it so much it physically hurts.

I know what I’m supposed to feel. I’m supposed to feel proud, right? The lucky guy with the stunning woman on his arm. I’m supposed to puff my chest out and walk tall. But every glance from a stranger feels like a hand reaching out to touch something that belongs to my soul. It feels like theft. Every pair of eyes on you is a threat. 

I catch myself having this thought… this terrible, shameful thought. It makes me sick, but it won’t leave my head. 

I wish you were ugly. 

*(He leans in a bit closer, whispering, his tone dropping into something desperate and fiercely intimate.)*

I wish the rest of the world looked at you and saw nothing. I wish your hair was dull, your skin was flawed, your voice grated on everyone else’s ears. I wish you were completely, undeniably unremarkable to every single person on this earth. 

Because if you were invisible to them… they would leave you alone. 

They wouldn’t look at you like you’re a prize to be won. No one would try to make you smile in the grocery store aisle. No one would secretly dream about you. You’d be safe. I could wrap you up in my coat, pull you through the crowds, and not a single soul would ever try to reach into our life and pull you away. 

And the part that terrifies me most? If you were hideous to the rest of the world, it wouldn’t change a single damn thing for me. 

I would still burn for you. I would still memorize every line of your face. I’d still fall to my knees just to breathe you in. If the whole world turned its back on you in disgust, I would just pull you into the dark, lock the door, and thank God that everyone else was too blind to see what I have. I’d keep you all to myself, like a dragon hiding gold in a cave.

*(He pauses, rubbing his temples, a wave of guilt washing over him.)*

It’s insane, isn’t it? It’s monstrous. You were built for the light. You deserve to be adored. You deserve to walk into a room and have the sun follow you. And here I am, secretly praying for the world to turn grey just so I don't have to share the view. Love isn’t supposed to make a man this greedy. It’s not supposed to make me want to hide you from the sun.

*(He finally lets his fingers gently trace her jawline, brushing a strand of hair from her face.)*

But tomorrow, the sun is going to come up. You’ll get dressed, you’ll walk out that door, and the world is going to stare at you all over again. And I’ll stand beside you, and I’ll smile, and I’ll play the proud man. 

But tonight… the doors are locked. The blinds are drawn. The world is outside. 

And for just a few hours… you’re mine. Only mine.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a short text using 2nd person POV ("you") about a mysterious woman sneaking out at night. Make the narrator sound desperate, proud, absurd, and deeply in love. Include odd sensory details like glasses, doctor visits, and bouillabaisse.
counterfactuals.output:
You think you are a shadow, my darling, but you navigate the dark with all the stealth of a runaway locomotive, and God help me, I have never seen anything more breathtaking. Look at you, adjusting those absurdly thick glasses in the moonlight—the left lens catches the streetlamp just so, turning you into a magnificent, one-eyed goddess of treason. 

My heart is shredding itself to ribbons! Where are you going at 3:00 AM? Please don't leave me! Yet look how brilliantly you step over the squeaky floorboard—the very knee that stumped three different specialists during those five agonizing doctor visits last autumn. Those fools called your joints a medical mystery, but they didn't understand your majesty; your cartilage clicks with the rhythmic precision of a grand grandfather clock! I am weeping into the mattress, paralyzed by terror that you will vanish forever, yet I am practically bursting with grand, ugly pride. 

You pause at the window sill, a shadowy phantom wrapped in a trench coat, exhaling a cloud that smells faintly and inexplicably of saffron, stewed cod, and garlic—the glorious, oily ghosts of tonight’s bouillabaisse still clinging to your collar. You are a genius! A criminal! A culinary enigma! 

I am suffocating in my love for you as you swing your leg over the ledge. Go, my impossible creature, conquer the night—just please, *please* come back before dawn!
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a modern literary excerpt exploring toxic devotion, body transformations, and the agonizing fear of abandonment.
counterfactuals.output:
The heat under my skin was not a fever; it was an architecture rearranging itself. 

It began in the shoulders. Julian had offhandedly mentioned, while tracing the line of my collarbone with a thumb that smelled faintly of salt and nicotine, that he preferred things that didn't crowd a room. He liked small, quiet geometry. So, that night, while he slept with his back turned—a pale wall of muscle that already felt miles away—I laid in the dark and willed my bones to yield. 

By dawn, my ribcage had knit itself three inches tighter. It hurt—a wet, dull aching deep in the marrow, like wet wood splintering—but when I breathed, I made no sound at all. I was smaller for him. I was becoming an whisper he could keep in his coat pocket.

"You look different," Julian said three days later, not looking up from his phone. His thumb swiped rhythmically across the glowing screen, a lazy, indifferent cadence that set my pulse hammering against the newly narrowed cage of my chest. 

"Do I?" My voice came out thinner, light as ash. I had dissolved my vocal cords slightly the night before, softening the harsh edges of my consonants because he once complained that my laugh startled him. 

"Maybe it’s the light," he murmured, his gaze drifting toward the window, toward the street below, toward the vast, terrifying world where thousands of people existed who were not me—people who did not require his permission to occupy space, people he might one day prefer.

The terror hit me then, cold and liquid, pooling in the back of my throat. It was the familiar black panic: the vision of his shoes by the front door, gone; the smell of his cedar cologne fading from the pillowcases; the unbearable, suffocating silence of an empty apartment where I would be left behind, a discarded draft of a person.

If he left, I would simply evaporate. There was no *me* prior to the shape of his hands.

That evening, I stood before the bathroom mirror, hands trembling against the cool porcelain of the sink. He had looked at a woman on the subway earlier—a girl with eyes like dark glass and hair the color of bruised plums. I closed my eyes and reached deep into the wet, pliable clay of my own biology. 

I felt the pigment shifting under my scalp, the follicles burning as they darkened, heavy and slick. My irises bled out their amber, muddying into an obsidian so dense it swallowed the vanity light. Pain flared behind my sockets, a sharp, blinding migraine of compliance, but I welcomed it. Pain was just the tax I paid to remain relevant to him. 

*Look at me,* I prayed into the mirror, my newly altered face staring back—a stranger’s face, stitched together from his fleeting glances at others. *Look at me and never look away again.*

When I stepped into the bedroom, Julian was sitting on the edge of the mattress, unlacing his boots. He stopped when he saw me. For a second, just a fraction of a second, his eyes widened. A flicker of shock, perhaps even revulsion, crossed his features before settling back into his chronic, terrifying boredom.

"What did you do to your hair?" he asked, his voice flat.

I crossed the room on feet I had flattened so my gait would sound like nothing at all. I sank to my knees before him, placing my hands on his knees. My skin was hot, still vibrating with the slow, agonized mutation of my spine bending to match the slope of his lap. 

"Whatever you want," I whispered, reaching up to take his heavy wrist, pressing his palm flat against my cheek. I felt my skin soften beneath his pressure, yielding to the exact impression of his fingers, ready to hold his shape forever. "Anything. Just tell me what to be."

He looked down at me, his expression unreadable, a man staring at a dog that had learned to speak in a human tongue. He didn't pull his hand away, but he didn't close his fingers around mine, either. And in that suspended, agonizing space between his touch and his withdrawal, I felt my body begin to loosen again, ready to tear itself apart at the seams just to build him a shelter he might decide to stay in.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
